79. Word Search

Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid.

\n\n

The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once.
input_format: A 2D character board and a word string.
constraints: board and word consist of only lowercase and uppercase English letters.
explanation: DFS backtracking from each cell. Mark cells as visited during search, then restore.

boilerplate.python:
import sys, json

def exist(board, word):
    m, n = len(board), len(board[0])
    def dfs(i, j, k):
        if k == len(word): return True
        if not (0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n) or board[i][j] != word[k]: return False
        tmp, board[i][j] = board[i][j], '#'
        res = any(dfs(i+di, j+dj, k+1) for di,dj in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)])
        board[i][j] = tmp
        return res
    return any(dfs(i, j, 0) for i in range(m) for j in range(n))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split('\n')
    if len(data) >= 2:
        board = json.loads(data[0])
        word = json.loads(data[1])
        print(json.dumps(exist(board, word)))
